verdict.rationale: Kimi's API Platform lets you create multiple API keys inside isolated projects. Each project carries its own budget, rate limits, IP whitelist and membership, and the Admin API manages inference keys programmatically, so you can confine an agent's credential to a narrowly bounded project. Restrictions attach to projects rather than to individual keys, and the docs never claim per-key permission scopes. missing for 10: per-key permission/endpoint scopes, agent-specific credential issuance (e.g., short-lived or delegated tokens), independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: You can create multiple projects in an organization and multiple API keys in each project
set project budgets and rate limits, manage members, configure an IP whitelist, and review organization and project consumption
The Kimi Admin API lets organization administrators manage members, invitations, projects, and inference API keys programmatically
Kimi members can create and manage API Keys in the Kimi Code Console
